name: hot_all_day_no_nat_vent_window
description: Outdoor is already above indoor from the start of the day. Hot-day classification (forecast high 92 / low 74, consistent with the 72-79F readings) fires at 6 AM with outdoor=76F > indoor=72F. A sensor_open event immediately enters pause (not nat vent) because outdoor >= indoor would add heat. No natural_ventilation outcome fires at any point.
notes: Covers the 'no nat-vent window' pattern: outdoor above indoor all day.
On days where outdoor is already warmer than indoor, opening windows adds heat rather than cooling.
The nat-vent activation guard (outdoor < indoor) prevents nat vent even when windows are opened.
The hot-day classification (hvac_mode=cool) is applied; indoor stays inside the comfort band so no cooling is needed, and the user has no beneficial window-open time.
Pairs with hot_all_day cases where ceiling guard would fire (modeled in Group B).

events.note: Already warm: outdoor=76F above indoor=72F before sunrise.
Hot-day classification (forecast high 92 / low 74): the classifier gives hvac_mode=cool and never recommends windows on a hot day (outdoor already above indoor).
Mid-morning: outdoor 79F, indoor 73F. Outdoor continues climbing above indoor.
User opens a window despite warm outdoor — outdoor 79F > indoor 73F should trigger pause, not nat vent.

assertions.reason: Hot-day classification applied: hvac_mode=cool. Indoor=72F is inside the comfort band (70-74F).
sensor_open with outdoor 79F >= indoor 73F — opening windows would import hotter air; nat-vent correctly does not activate (nat_vent_not_active). HVAC idle, nothing to pause.
All sensors closed — automation resumes from pause.

verdict.summary: When outdoor is above indoor all day, window-open events enter pause not nat vent; no natural_ventilation fires
verdict.observed_behavior: classification_applied (hot, cool) → paused on window open → resumed on window close
verdict.expected_behavior: Pause when outdoor >= indoor; nat vent guard correctly suppressed all day
